oe.title: Determining the purity of salbutamol with analytical techniques
points: Melting point: a pure sample melts sharply over a narrow range at the literature value; impurities lower it and broaden the range. Mixed melting point with an authentic sample gives no depression if pure.
TLC: a single spot with the same R_f as pure salbutamol (co-spot); extra spots show impurities or unreacted starting material.
IR: should show O–H (3600–3200 cm^−1), N–H, aromatic C–H, and no C=O peak (the ketone/ester intermediates are fully reduced). An extra C=O peak shows impurity.
^1H NMR: correct number of environments, integration ratio and splitting; extra peaks show impurities.
Mass spectrometry: molecular ion at m/z 239 (C_13H_21NO_3); fragment peaks match the structure.
Elemental microanalysis: % C, H, N should match the formula. Also HPLC/GC to measure percentage purity.
equations: R_f = distance moved by spot / distance moved by solvent front
diagrams: TLC plate with sample, pure standard and co-spot.
Sketch IR spectrum labelling the O–H/N–H region and the absence of C=O at ~1700 cm^−1.
Melting point apparatus with a note on sharp vs broad melting.

oe.title: Reactions of benzene, cyclohexene and cyclohexane
points: Cyclohexane: saturated (sp^3, σ bonds only) and unreactive apart from combustion and free-radical substitution with halogens in UV light (initiation, propagation, termination).

Cyclohexene: C=C (σ + π bond) undergoes electrophilic addition. It rapidly decolourises bromine water (test for unsaturation) and also adds HX, H_2O (acid catalyst), and H_2 (Ni/Pt catalyst) → cyclohexane.
Benzene: planar ring, sp^2 carbons with a delocalised π system (6 electrons) giving extra stability, so it resists addition and doesn't decolourise bromine water.

Benzene undergoes electrophilic substitution, keeping the aromatic ring: halogenation (Br_2/FeBr_3), nitration (conc HNO_3/H_2SO_4, NO_2^+), sulfonation (SO_3/H_2SO_4), Friedel–Crafts alkylation (RCl/AlCl_3).
All three burn (benzene with a sooty flame, high C:H ratio).
Mechanisms: addition goes via a carbocation (or cyclic bromonium ion); substitution via an intermediate where the ring's delocalisation is temporarily disrupted, then H^+ is lost.
equations: C_6H_6 + HNO_3 → C_6H_5NO_2 + H_2O (H_2SO_4 catalyst, NO_2^+ electrophile)
diagrams: Curly-arrow mechanism for electrophilic addition of Br_2 to cyclohexene.
Curly-arrow mechanism for nitration of benzene.
Sketch of benzene's delocalised π cloud vs a localised C=C.
